hints: Determine the class boundaries and class widths in thousands: $2.5\text{ to } 7.5$ (width 5), $7.5\text{ to } 12.5$ (width 5), $12.5\text{ to } 22.5$ (width 10), $22.5\text{ to } 42.5$ (width 20), $42.5\text{ to } 82.5$ (width 40).
Calculate the frequency density for each class using $\text{Frequency Density} = \dfrac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class Width}}$.
Draw bars on the specified horizontal scale (2 cm per 10 000) with vertical axis labeled 'Frequency density'.
walkthrough:
Determine the continuous class boundaries and class widths (in thousands):
- Class 3000 to 7000: boundaries $2.5$ to $7.5$, width $5$
- Class 8000 to 12 000: boundaries $7.5$ to $12.5$, width $5$
- Class 13 000 to 22 000: boundaries $12.5$ to $22.5$, width $10$
- Class 23 000 to 42 000: boundaries $22.5$ to $42.5$, width $20$
- Class 43 000 to 82 000: boundaries $42.5$ to $82.5$, width $40$

Calculate the frequency density for each class using $\text{FD} = \dfrac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class width}}$:
$$\text{FD}_1 = \dfrac{40}{5} = 8$$
$$\text{FD}_2 = \dfrac{30}{5} = 6$$
$$\text{FD}_3 = \dfrac{18}{10} = 1.8$$
$$\text{FD}_4 = \dfrac{34}{20} = 1.7$$
$$\text{FD}_5 = \dfrac{8}{40} = 0.2$$
Draw the histogram on graph paper with horizontal axis 'Capacity (thousands)' using 2 cm for 10 000, and vertical axis 'Frequency density' from 0 to 8.

ai_rubric.Constructing Histograms: Draws bars with the stated class boundaries and correct frequency-density heights.
ai_rubric.Calculating Frequency Density: Uses frequency divided by class width for each histogram class.

teacher_walkthrough:
To draw a histogram with unequal class widths, the height of each bar must represent the frequency density, calculated as:
$$\text{Frequency Density} = \frac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class Width}}$$

First, establish the continuous class boundaries from the discrete capacity ranges (given to the nearest thousand):
- 3000 to 7000: boundaries are $2500$ to $7500$ $\implies$ width $= 5000$ (or $5$ thousand)
- 8000 to 12 000: boundaries are $7500$ to $12500$ $\implies$ width $= 5000$ (or $5$ thousand)
- 13 000 to 22 000: boundaries are $12500$ to $22500$ $\implies$ width $= 10000$ (or $10$ thousand)
- 23 000 to 42 000: boundaries are $22500$ to $42500$ $\implies$ width $= 20000$ (or $20$ thousand)
- 43 000 to 82 000: boundaries are $42500$ to $82500$ $\implies$ width $= 40000$ (or $40$ thousand)

Calculate the frequency density (per thousand) for each bar:
$$\text{Bar 1: } \frac{40}{5} = 8$$
$$\text{Bar 2: } \frac{30}{5} = 6$$
$$\text{Bar 3: } \frac{18}{10} = 1.8$$
$$\text{Bar 4: } \frac{34}{20} = 1.7$$
$$\text{Bar 5: } \frac{8}{40} = 0.2$$

Plot on graph paper:
- Horizontal axis: 'Capacity (thousands)' using 2 cm for 10 000, spanning from 0 to at least 85.
- Vertical axis: 'Frequency density' starting linearly at 0 and reaching up to 8.
- Draw adjacent bars between the continuous boundaries with the computed heights.

skill_tags: Estimating a Mean from Grouped Data

hints: Find the midpoint $x$ for each class in thousands: 5, 10, 17.5, 32.5, 62.5.
Multiply each midpoint by its class frequency to find $\sum f x$.
Divide $\sum f x$ by the total number of stadiums ($n = 130$).
walkthrough:
Identify class midpoints $x$ (in thousands):
- Class 3000 to 7000: midpoint $x_1 = 5$
- Class 8000 to 12 000: midpoint $x_2 = 10$
- Class 13 000 to 22 000: midpoint $x_3 = 17.5$
- Class 23 000 to 42 000: midpoint $x_4 = 32.5$
- Class 43 000 to 82 000: midpoint $x_5 = 62.5$

Calculate $\sum f x$:
$$\sum f x = (40 \times 5) + (30 \times 10) + (18 \times 17.5) + (34 \times 32.5) + (8 \times 62.5)$$
$$\sum f x = 200 + 300 + 315 + 1105 + 500 = 2420\text{ thousand}$$

Divide by the total frequency $n = 130$ to estimate the mean:
$$\bar{x} = \dfrac{2420}{130} = \dfrac{242}{13} \approx 18.6\text{ thousand (or } 18600\text{)}$$

ai_rubric.Estimating a Mean from Grouped Data: Uses class midpoints and frequencies in the grouped-mean calculation.

teacher_walkthrough:
To estimate the mean of grouped data, find the midpoint $x$ of each class interval:
- Class 1 (2.5 to 7.5): $x_1 = \frac{2.5 + 7.5}{2} = 5$
- Class 2 (7.5 to 12.5): $x_2 = \frac{7.5 + 12.5}{2} = 10$
- Class 3 (12.5 to 22.5): $x_3 = \frac{12.5 + 22.5}{2} = 17.5$
- Class 4 (22.5 to 42.5): $x_4 = \frac{22.5 + 42.5}{2} = 32.5$
- Class 5 (42.5 to 82.5): $x_5 = \frac{42.5 + 82.5}{2} = 62.5$

Multiply each class frequency $f$ by its midpoint $x$:
$$40 \times 5 = 200$$
$$30 \times 10 = 300$$
$$18 \times 17.5 = 315$$
$$34 \times 32.5 = 1105$$
$$8 \times 62.5 = 500$$

Sum all $f x$ products:
$$\sum f x = 200 + 300 + 315 + 1105 + 500 = 2420\text{ thousand}$$

Divide by the total number of stadiums $N = 130$:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{\sum f x}{N} = \frac{2420}{130} = \frac{242}{13} \approx 18.615$$
Rounded to 3 significant figures, the estimated mean capacity is $18.6$ thousand (or $18600$ people).

hints: Form the cumulative frequencies for the classes: 40, 70, 88, 122, 130.
Find the rank of the median: $\dfrac{130}{2} = 65\text{th}$ stadium. Identify the class containing this value.
Find the rank of the lower quartile: $\dfrac{130}{4} = 32.5\text{th}$ stadium. Identify the class containing this value.
walkthrough:
Compute the running cumulative frequencies for the five classes:
- Up to 7000: $40$
- Up to 12 000: $40 + 30 = 70$
- Up to 22 000: $70 + 18 = 88$
- Up to 42 000: $88 + 34 = 122$
- Up to 82 000: $122 + 8 = 130$

Locate the median at the $\frac{130}{2} = 65\text{th}$ observation:
$$\text{Since } 40 < 65 \le 70, \text{ the median is in the class } 8000\text{ to } 12\,000$$

Locate the lower quartile at the $\frac{130}{4} = 32.5\text{th}$ observation:
$$\text{Since } 32.5 \le 40, \text{ the lower quartile is in the class } 3000\text{ to } 7000$$

ai_rubric.Finding Medians and Quartiles: Locates the required median or quartile from the ordered or grouped data.

teacher_walkthrough:
To identify which class intervals contain the median and lower quartile, calculate the cumulative frequencies across the classes:
1. Class 3000 to 7000: frequency $= 40 \implies \text{cumulative frequency} = 40$
2. Class 8000 to 12 000: frequency $= 30 \implies \text{cumulative frequency} = 40 + 30 = 70$
3. Class 13 000 to 22 000: frequency $= 18 \implies \text{cumulative frequency} = 70 + 18 = 88$
4. Class 23 000 to 42 000: frequency $= 34 \implies \text{cumulative frequency} = 88 + 34 = 122$
5. Class 43 000 to 82 000: frequency $= 8 \implies \text{cumulative frequency} = 122 + 8 = 130$

Step 1: Locate the median class.
For grouped data with $N = 130$, the median position is:
$$\text{Median position} = \frac{130}{2} = 65\text{th stadium}$$
The first class accounts for items 1 to 40. The second class accounts for items 41 to 70. Since 65 falls between 41 and 70:
$$\text{Median class: } 8000\text{ to } 12\,000$$

Step 2: Locate the lower-quartile class.
The lower quartile position is:
$$\text{Lower quartile position} = \frac{130}{4} = 32.5\text{th stadium}$$
Because 32.5 is less than or equal to 40, it falls within the very first class:
$$\text{Lower-quartile class: } 3000\text{ to } 7000$$
